summary: Baij Nath Puri was an Indian scholar in indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1948-1950) and served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1971-1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak worked in indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1873-1874), Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1874-1877), and Government Law College, Mumbai (~1877-1879).

Bal Krishen Thapar was a scholar of history, archaeology, and indology. He studied at the University of the Punjab (~1941-1943) and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1978-1981).
Bala Sahai Shastri was an indologist. He held posts at Panjab University, where he served as an Assistant (attested 1932) and later as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1941).

Bangwei Wang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, indology, and sinology. After completing his doctoral dissertation at Peking University (~1983-1987), he became Professor and Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies there (~1993).
Banikanta Kakati worked in linguistics and indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1916-1918) and served as a professor at Cotton University (~1918-1947).

Barbara E. Ward was a scholar of sinology who studied at Newnham College (~1937-1940). She held posts at the University of London (~1948-1965), Newnham College (~1973-1978), and the University of Cambridge (~1973-1978).

Barbara Gerke is a tibetologist who earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (2011-2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.
Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar of tibetology and religious studies. She completed her studies at Queen's University (~1958-1962) and SOAS University of London (1969-1974).

Barbara Stoler Miller was an indologist who studied at Barnard, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD, ~1964-1968) under W. Norman Brown and Royal W. Weiler. She served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Studies at Barnard College (~1968-1993).

Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2001) under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying with G. Raj, and held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend Faddegon was a scholar of indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1894-1904) and later held a post there from 1907 to 1944.

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Leiden University, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1990-1992), and the University of Hamburg (~1992-2007) as Professor Dr.

Barend ter Haar is a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University (-1990) and held posts at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (attested 1994), Heidelberg University, and Leiden (attested 2002-2013).

Barry Kerzin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at UC Berkeley (~1969-1972), Keck School of Medicine of USC (~1972-1976), and under traditional teacher Geshe Namgyal Wangchen.

Barry Sautman works in sinology and tibetology. He studied at UCLA School of Law (~1971-1974), NYU School of Law (~1980-1981), and Columbia University (~1985-1990), later holding a post at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (~1993-2020).
Bart Dessein works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Willemen and served as Associate Professor at Ghent University (attested 2014-2019).
Basil Gould worked in tibetology and linguistics. After studying at Winchester College (~1896-1902) and New College (~1902-1906), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1907-1947).

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton (~1847-1849), the University of Bonn (~1851-1852), and under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl (~1851-1853). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University (~1876-1915).

Beata Grant is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning her Ph.D. at Stanford (~1980-1987) and a fellowship at UC Berkeley (~1987-1988), she was Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989-2021).
